themes.name: Enhancement of Critical Thinking through AI Integration
themes.definition: AI tools and educational frameworks are implemented to improve students' critical thinking abilities, as measured in various academic contexts through interventions and assessments.
evidence: [Liu2024a] AI tools can effectively enhance critical thinking abilities in English literature classes.
[Huang2025a] Enhancements were also observed in higher-order thinking skills domains, particularly in critical thinking, problem-solving, and creativity.
[Gholiagha2025] embedding AI into participatory, reflexive pedagogies can support the development of critical thinking by making the cultural and political dimensions of technology more visible.

themes.name: AI Literacy and Ethical Competence Development
themes.definition: Educational programs aim to develop students' proficiency in using AI tools, with emphasis on operational skills, ethical considerations, security, and critical evaluation, as framed in literacy frameworks and measured through scales.
evidence: [Zhang2025a] GenAI literacy framework that includes four dimensions: (a) Operational Competence in GenAI Tools, (b) Ethics and Security in GenAI Usage, (c) Critical Evaluation of GenAI Outputs and Autonomy and (d) Reflection in GenAI Application.
[Tseng2025] AI literacy was measured using the Meta AI Literacy Scale (MAILS).

[Wan2025] qualitative thematic analysis of student reflections supported these findings and highlighted four key themes: enhanced knowledge transfer, increased self-efficacy, critical engagement with AI, and ethical awareness.

themes.name: Higher-Order Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills Enhancement
themes.definition: AI applications are used to foster complex cognitive skills such as analysis, evaluation, creativity, and problem-solving in educational interventions, often assessed through surveys and experimental designs.
evidence: [Zhang2025b] relationship between higher-order thinking and problem-solving skills development among pre-service teachers using generative AI
[Du2025] AI slightly enhances the originality and usefulness of design sketches and significantly increases the number of HOTS used and the diversity of their interconnections.
[Omeh2025b] develop critical thinking skills, algorithm skills and problem-solving skills among others which are components of computational thinking.

themes.name: Metacognition and Reflective Learning Practices
themes.definition: AI-integrated activities support students' metacognitive awareness and reflective skills, often through reflection journals, feedback mechanisms, and collaborative sensemaking, leading to improved calibration and self-regulation.
evidence: [Asher2026] practice—regardless of feedback type—improved metacognitive calibration compared to lecture
[Hwang2025] enhanced students' critical thinking, metacognition and problem-solving tendencies
[Zhang2025a] Reflection journals, which promote critical thinking and metacognitive awareness

themes.name: Personalized and Adaptive Learning Environments
themes.definition: AI technologies facilitate learning experiences that are tailored to individual students' progress, needs, and preferences through adaptive pathways and personalized feedback, as implemented in various instructional models.
evidence: [Yao2025] adaptive personalized learning pathways
[Yavuz2025] personalized learning experiences
[Asher2026] personalized, AI-generated feedback elicited higher interest

themes.name: Student Engagement and Motivation
themes.definition: The use of AI tools in education leads to increased student involvement, interest, motivation, and emotional engagement in learning activities, measured through dimensions like behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement.
evidence: [Huang2025a] considerable improvements in the experimental group across behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement dimensions.
[Li2025b] AI-enhanced teaching stimulated motivation and self-efficacy
[Yavuz2025] positively influenced students’ motivation, interest in the course

themes.name: Critical Assessment of AI-Generated Content
themes.definition: Educational assignments require students to evaluate, fact-check, and critically analyze outputs from AI systems to develop evidence-based reasoning and skepticism, often through specific exercises or tools.
evidence: [MacNeil2025] help students think critically about autogenerated code suggestions
[Holzmann2025] teach students the importance of evaluating claims based on experimental evidence
[Pence2024] students evaluated the output using a critical thinking exercise

data.meta_observations: Many studies employ mixed-methods or quasi-experimental designs to assess AI interventions in education, with a common focus on measuring outcomes like critical thinking, AI literacy, and problem-solving. There is an emphasis on discipline-specific applications and ethical considerations across various fields such as nursing, engineering, and language learning.
data.grounding_notes: Themes are derived solely from verbatim text in the abstracts, with some abstracts having quality issues (e.g., missing methods or no quantitative data) that limit evidence. All article keys are from the provided closed set, and quotes are exact copies from the abstracts.
